headline: Stroud 10K about 37:20 on a net-uphill course, ahead of target and the model; achilles 0, HRV baseline drifting low, so hold and keep Guy Fawkes on feel.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 25 October 2026

Shep — Stroud is done and this goes out before you've logged it, so the race read below is from the watch only. Tell me the chip time, how the chest was, and what you took.

## Stroud 10K

**10.0 km on the watch in 37:20** (chip may differ by a few seconds). Target was ~37:30 with sub-38 the floor, so you beat it on a net-uphill course with an uphill finish. The model's flat figure was 37:20 and the course should have cost 15-25 s, so this is roughly that much *ahead* of the blended model. Same direction as 4 Oct and Cheltenham: my course penalties have now been too cautious three times running, and they get smaller next time.

Splits: 3:35, 3:47, 3:36, 3:40, 3:46, 3:46, 3:46, 3:49, 3:44, 3:51. HR built 155 to 170 and plateaued from km 5. First 5 km 18:25, second 18:55: a 30 s positive split on a course that climbs into km 7-8, which is the expected shape, not a fade. The opening 3:35 matched the plan rather than what the downhill offered, so the discipline held. My best read is 10K fitness around 37:00-37:15 flat, and that is the number that feeds the Manchester picture.

## The week

Planned: rest / 8 / 6x600 / 7 / 6+strides / rest / race. Done: 8.0, 12.4 (reps), 7.0, 6.3, a busy-day rest on Saturday (sensible), then the race. About 47 km before the cool-down, the lightest week of the month, as designed.

**21 Oct, 6x600:** 3:23, 3:36, 3:37, 3:29, 3:32, 3:30 against 3:32-3:36 (spread 14 s, `structured` reps). You said you muddled the first three paces: the 3:23 was nine seconds inside, 3:36-3:37 slightly outside, the last three right. Immaterial four days out, and RPE 6 at HR 154 is a good sign. Put the target on the watch next time. No chest symptoms logged at 10 C.

## Recovery and achilles

Achilles 0 every day, no first-step or desk-chair stiffness mentioned. Alphaflys on an easy run again (20 Oct), no reaction: still easy runs only.

The 7-day HRV baseline has drifted 38.8 to 35.6 over the fortnight. On the 24th RHR was 51 and HRV 33 (flagged), settling to 49 / 34 on race morning. Nothing in your notes explains it, so it is not a dip I can excuse. It follows a 65 km fortnight-peak with two hard sessions, and it is not alarming: RHR is back in range and the race was good. What matters is the week after Stroud, when the baseline should recover. If it is still sliding by Friday, that is fatigue whatever the cause.

## Looking ahead

- **Guy Fawkes 5, 1 Nov** stays an experiment, raced on feel. A week is short after a 10K at this effort. Friday gate: baseline still sliding, or RHR 51+ with no reason, makes it a steady run; a temperature or aches means no race. If you feel fine you can overrule the numbers: say so and I'll restore it.
- **Fission 20 entries open about 1 Nov and sell out every year.** Enter that week if you want the March rehearsal.
- **Asthma:** you planned to raise the 17 Oct cold-air chest tightness with your GP or asthma nurse after Stroud. That is now. Bring the date, 6-7 C, 2x15 min threshold, last ~3 min, both inhalers taken beforehand, settled on stopping. Reliever before cold sessions and the winter preventer are their decision.
- **November build** starts after Guy Fawkes: 2-8 Nov ~62 km, Tuesday 12, first 18 km long run with gels, no quality. In 9-15 Nov an interval session and the Saturday tempo return with volume held at ~64 km and the long run held at 18, so volume and intensity do not rise together.

## Recommendation

**Hold.** The race week and race went as designed. Changes are only firming this week and extending the horizon to 15 Nov.

athlete_response.thoughts:
Tomorrow's session, about 8 km all in (the same as the planned easy run):
Warm-up: 3 km easy, with a buff if it's cold, finishing with 3–4 pickups.
Main set: 6–8 × 200 m at 3:30–3:35/km, which is 42–43 s per rep.
Recovery: 200 m slow jog, or about 90 s–2 min. Full recovery is the point: each rep should feel as easy as the first.
Cool-down: 2–3 km easy.

coach_reply:
Shep — yes, this holds up, and I've proposed it for your approval.

**Why it's fine:** 6–8 × 200 m at 3:30–3:35 is about 25 s of work per rep with full recovery. That is neuromuscular speed work, not a hard session: little lactate, little recovery cost. Wednesday is three days after Stroud and the numbers don't argue against it: RHR 47 on Monday (down from 51 on the 24th), HRV 34 against a 35 baseline, achilles 0 throughout. It also gives you some leg speed before Guy Fawkes, which has no other sharpening this week.

**Two adjustments:** I've dropped Thursday's 4 strides so you aren't adding speed twice in 48 hours. And keep the reps *on* 42–43 s, not under. Last week's 3:23 first rep was nine seconds inside target; the point here is that rep 1 and rep 8 look identical. Wear the Speed 5, not the Alphafly. Stop at 6 if the legs feel heavy, and log any chest tightness, since it will be cold.

**What doesn't change:** the Friday gate for Sunday. If the baseline is still sliding or RHR is 51+ with no reason, Guy Fawkes becomes a steady run. Approve the proposal and it lands on the plan.
